slot.brief: Ask which compound is obtained when a Grignard reagent reacts with a specified substrate (water/CO2/methanol) or which reagent destroys a Grignard reagent; simple product identification.

stem: What is formed after hydrolysis of the product obtained by reacting $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{MgBr}$ with $\text{CO}_2$?

verdicts.working: C₂H₅MgBr reacts with CO₂ to form a carboxylate with one extra carbon; hydrolysis gives CH₃CH₂COOH, propanoic acid.

working:
$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{MgBr}+\text{CO}_2\rightarrow\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{CO}_2\text{MgBr}$\nHydrolysis gives $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COOH}$ (propanoic acid).

Independent check: C₂H₅MgBr reacts with CO₂ to form a carboxylate with one extra carbon; hydrolysis gives CH₃CH₂COOH, propanoic acid.
solution:
Grignard reagents react with $\text{CO}_2$ to form a carboxylate with one additional carbon atom.
$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{MgBr}+\text{CO}_2\rightarrow\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{CO}_2\text{MgBr}\xrightarrow{\text{hydrolysis}}\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COOH}$$
The product is propanoic acid.
